ranges.format: MET-<layer><NNN> — layer is a single letter, NNN is a zero-padded 3-digit sequence within that layer.

layers.F: foundation — internal/foundation/* (registry, correlation IDs, logging, determinism, serialization, solver, build info)
layers.T: tooling — build/plan/generate scripts (currently JS, outside the Go registry)

reserved.F000-F009: errs package self-errors (registry load/validation, unregistered code) — always available even if the registry fails to load

ranges.toolingNote: tools/plan/generate.js currently raises inline string codes MET-T001..MET-T030 (see its header comment) and is NOT wired to this registry — it runs before code.json/data/errors.json can be trusted to exist. Migrating it to read data/errors.json (or a generated tooling subset) is future work; do not remove or renumber its inline codes without updating this note and the script together.

MET-F001.message: error registry failed to load from {path}: {cause}
MET-F001.remedy: Check that data/errors.json exists, is valid JSON, and passes schema validation (unique codes, required fields, MET-<layer><NNN> format). Set METROPOLIS_ERRORS_PATH to override the resolved path if it was found in the wrong place.

MET-F002.remedy: Fix the offending entry in data/errors.json (duplicate code, bad code format, or missing severity/module/message/remedy field) and reload.

MET-F003.remedy: Add {code} to data/errors.json before using it — GR#7 forbids ad-hoc error construction. This wrapper error is itself always available even if the registry failed to load, so the failure is never silent.

MET-F004.message: correlation ID missing or empty when constructing error {code}
MET-F004.remedy: Every errs.New/errs.Wrap call must carry a non-empty correlation ID. Mint one with errs.NewCorrelationID() at the boundary (protocol command, CLI invocation, test setup) and propagate it through the call chain.

MET-F010.message: failed to write NDJSON log entry to {path}: {cause}
MET-F010.remedy: Check disk space and file permissions on the logs/ directory. The error is still retained in the in-memory ring buffer (Recent()) even when the write fails.

MET-F011.remedy: Check that logs/ is writable and that rotated files (.1, .2, .3) are not locked by another process. Logging continues to the current file uncapped until rotation succeeds.

MET-F012.message: cannot open log file {path} for writing: {cause}
MET-F012.remedy: Ensure the logs/ directory exists and is writable, or set an explicit writer via NewLogger. Falls back to the in-memory ring buffer sink so errors are never printed-and-lost.

MET-F013.message: malformed log entry could not be marshalled to JSON: {cause}
MET-F013.remedy: Ensure ctx values passed to errs.New/Wrap are JSON-marshalable (no channels, funcs, or cyclic structures).

MET-F020.remedy: Correlation IDs must be UUIDv4-formatted strings minted by errs.NewCorrelationID(). Do not hand-construct correlation IDs.
